status_summary: CEQ removed its government-wide NEPA regulations by an interim final rule (90 FR 10610, published 2025-02-25, effective 2025-04-11) and finalized the removal on 2026-01-08 (91 FR 618). Interior published an interim final rule on 2025-07-03 and a final rule on 2026-02-24 (91 FR 8738), relying on the Supreme Court's 2025 Seven County decision, that removes most of its NEPA procedures from 43 CFR part 46 and moves them to a non-codified handbook (February 2026 version); the handbook sets a 75-page limit for environmental assessments and 150 pages (300 for extraordinarily complex actions) for impact statements, with one-year and two-year completion limits (180 days and one year where an expedited review fee is paid), and a requirement to show preparation cost on the first page was not found in the text read. Interior announced two BLM categorical exclusions for timber salvage and thinning on 2026-08-20; the notices were published and took effect on 2026-08-24, and a further categorical exclusion for wintertime oil and gas exploration in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska took effect on 2026-10-09. The design differs from the Mandate, which asked to reinstate the 2020 CEQ rules and secretarial orders, and no congressional change to NEPA judicial review was found.

timeline.event: CEQ publishes an interim final rule (90 FR 10610) removing its NEPA implementing regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations and requesting comment; it takes effect 2025-04-11 (next entry).
CEQ's interim final rule removing its NEPA implementing regulations takes effect (effective date stated in the rule published 2025-02-25).
Interior publishes an interim final rule, National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Regulations, with a 30-day comment period (description from Interior's 2026 final rule).
Center for Biological Diversity and Sierra Club sue in the Northern District of California to vacate Interior's July 2025 NEPA interim final rule (month only; first of month used).

CEQ publishes a final rule (91 FR 618, effective the same day) removing its NEPA implementing regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations; it adopts the February 2025 interim final rule as final without changes.

Interior publishes its final NEPA rule, effective the same day: most procedures leave 43 CFR part 46 for a handbook, while emergency response, categorical exclusions, applicant-prepared documents and lead and cooperating agency provisions stay in regulation.

Interior publishes notices of two finalized BLM NEPA categorical exclusions, timber salvage harvest (91 FR 54739) and forest and woodland density management, effective on publication (announced 2026-08-20); salvage harvest is capped at 1,000 acres where the disturbance covers 3,000 acres or less, otherwise at the lesser of 5,000 acres or one third of the disturbance area.
Interior establishes, effective on publication, a categorical exclusion in its NEPA Handbook for BLM wintertime oil and gas exploration in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska (91 FR 64673).
